mappings.note: Excluding the practice that does not conserve water is using resources judiciously, LO-13's own wording. Not LO-12, because the item is about protecting the supply rather than treating water for use.
Potable water as water fit to drink belongs to the purifying-water application in LO-12. Not LO-13, which covers conserving the resource rather than making it drinkable.
Naming environmental contamination as pollution is hazard terminology under the environmental outcome. Not LO-4, because no particular cause or effect is traced.
Defining pollutants as the agents that contaminate air, water and soil is the same hazard terminology. Not LO-2, because the item defines rather than sorts.
The proportion of oxygen in air is the composition of a material, covered by LO-1's properties and structure. Not LO-13, because no hazard is involved.
Excluding the gas that is not a greenhouse gas sorts materials by a property. Not LO-4, used here for the warming mechanism rather than the membership question.
The July tree-planting drive, Van Mahotsav, is an organised effort to protect the environment. Not LO-12, because it is a public programme rather than a household practice.
The procedure giving water free of all impurities is water purification, named verbatim in LO-12. Not LO-3, because the method is recalled rather than investigated.
The nitrogen percentage of air is a composition fact about a material. Grouped with the oxygen-percentage item for the same reason.
Which gases cause acid rain links pollutants to the acid-rain phenomenon LO-4 names. Not LO-2, because the gases are traced to an effect rather than classified.
Identifying a respiratory disease sits in the chain from air pollutants to health effects that LO-4 covers. Not LO-13, because no protective measure is proposed.
Eutrophication depleting dissolved oxygen relates a phenomenon to its consequence. Not LO-13, since no remedy is asked for.
What CFCs turn ozone into is the mechanism of ozone depletion, a phenomenon and its cause. Not LO-6, whose equations are confined to metals and non-metals with air, water and acids.
What is chiefly damaging the Taj Mahal is the monument-deterioration example in LO-4. Duplicate in substance of the earlier Taj Mahal items.
The oxygen percentage of air is a material composition fact. Duplicate of the earlier oxygen item and coded the same way.
What causes water pollution relates the problem to its sources. Not LO-12, because no purification follows.
Knowing which river is the most polluted is awareness of an environmental hazard. Not LO-4, because no cause or mechanism is named.

The gas that causes global warming is phrased causally and therefore sits on the relate-to-cause outcome. Deliberately different from the membership items, which ask which gases count as greenhouse gases and take LO-2.
Finding the wrongly matched pollutant and effect is pollutant-to-effect reasoning across a whole table. Not LO-2, because the pairing, not the class, is tested.
Excluding what does not cause air pollution is cause identification. Not LO-13, since no protective action is proposed.
Identifying the gas associated with the greenhouse effect is a membership question about a class of gases. Grouped with the other greenhouse-gas classification items rather than the mechanism items.
Carbon particles and factory smoke producing smog is the smog-formation example LO-4 names word for word. Not LO-13, because the outcome is described rather than prevented.
Which gases produce acid rain links pollutants to the phenomenon. Duplicate in substance of the earlier acid-rain item.
Trapped reflected heat identified as the greenhouse effect names a phenomenon from its mechanism. Not LO-2, because no gas is being classified.
